questions.question: When your driver license expires, what can you do?

options.text: Drive during a 90-day grace period.
Drive as long as a licensed driver is with you.
Renew your license within one year of expiration, but you cannot drive with an expired license.
Drive to and from work only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Renew your license within one year of expiration, but you cannot drive with an expired license.
questions.explanation: Your license is void after it expires. There is no grace period. You can renew it within one year of the expiration date, but you cannot drive with an expired license.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Speed up.
Stop completely.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and continue with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and continue with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard. Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.question: How should you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly to check traffic.
Always stop completely first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering a freeway, signal and match the speed of traffic. Always yield to other vehicles.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to increase distance between you.
Brake suddenly to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to spot tailgaters. If someone is following too closely, slow down and let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: You reach an intersection with a flashing red light. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when safe.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Stop only if other cars are in the intersection.
Slow down and stop only if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop, give the right-of-way to others, and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line. This tells you that:

options.text: The road has traffic going both directions.
The road is one-way.
The road is under repair.
You must stay left of the broken yellow lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road has traffic going both directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken line means you can cross it to pass when safe.

questions.question: When driving in rain, you must use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
No lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in rain.

questions.question: As you approach an intersection, the light turns from green to yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Brake hard to stop.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Be prepared to stop before the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, you should:

options.text: Try to drive faster than the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is near.
Look for a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no trains are nearby and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is near.
questions.explanation: Railroad warning signs tell you a train might be coming. Obey all warning signs and never go around barriers.

questions.question: How can you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn just before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder to see if your blind spot is clear. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red signals and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires properly maintained.
Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Watch for standing water or puddles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, your car takes longer to stop and may skid on sharp turns. Do not use cruise control in wet or icy conditions. Reduce your speed and drive carefully.

questions.question: When entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp, a driver should:

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
Have the right-of-way.
Force their way into traffic.
Assume other drivers will change lanes for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When entering from an entrance or acceleration ramp, you must yield to drivers already on the interstate. Merge safely into traffic when it is possible to do so.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: Merging traffic
Proceed with caution.
Pedestrian crossing
Come to a full stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive carefully and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign mean?

options.text: The start of a no passing zone.
A railroad crossing is ahead.
A school zone is ahead.
Construction work is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work is ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn drivers about construction, maintenance, or emergency work. They have black symbols on them.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid lines mean you cannot pass.

questions.question: When can you cross a solid yellow line?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed, but solid lines cannot. You may cross a solid yellow line only when turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must travel at this exact speed.
The highest legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
You must travel through intersections at this speed.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This is a speed limit sign. It shows the maximum speed allowed on that road. In rain, snow, ice, or poor conditions, you should drive slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: Larger blind spots.
Smaller blind spots.
No blind spots.
The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Larger blind spots.
questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have bigger blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near their rears that cannot be seen in side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give as much space as possible.
Speed up and pull in front of the bicyclist quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and give them plenty of space. Bicyclists have less protection than car drivers. Passing too quickly can cause them to lose control.

questions.question: You are driving forward out of your driveway. What must you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop before crossing the sidewalk.
Slow down before crossing the sidewalk.
Have the right-of-way over pedestrians on the sidewalk.
Cross the sidewalk without stopping if you honk your horn first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop before crossing the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: When driving out of a driveway, always stop completely before entering the road. Stop before crossing the sidewalk. Failing to stop is against the law.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals. Which one has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car approaching from the right.
The car approaching from the left.
The car whose driver sounds the horn first.
The car traveling the fastest.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car approaching from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection of two similar roads with no traffic signals, you must yield to the vehicle approaching from your right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street the wrong way.
School crossing ahead.
Do not drive in this lane.
Drivers turning left on green must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers turning left on green must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign is used with a traffic light to tell drivers that left-turning traffic does not have the right-of-way. Wait for oncoming traffic to pass before turning.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes unclear.
You become less alert.
You calm down and concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your ability to see clearly, affects your judgment of speed and distance, reduces your ability to recover from headlight glare, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: On slippery roads, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down.
Drive faster.
Drive at the speed limit with caution.
Never drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down as soon as you see rain, snow, or ice on the road. These conditions create slippery surfaces. You may need to drive slower than the posted speed limit for safety.

questions.question: A steady green light at an intersection means you:

options.text: Must slow down and prepare to stop.
Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.
May drive through if the road is clear.
Cannot turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: May drive through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can drive through the intersection if the road is clear. You may also turn right or left on green unless a sign prohibits the turn. Always yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The right lane ends and traffic should merge left.
The road curves ahead.
Intersections are coming up.
Road construction is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and traffic should merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the right lane on the road will end. Traffic in the right lane must move left.

questions.question: Which traffic light means you should slow down and proceed carefully at an intersection?

options.text: A flashing yellow light
A flashing red light
A solid yellow light
A solid red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, proceed with caution, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Very uncommon.
Extremely risky.
Nothing to worry about.
No more dangerous than normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Extremely risky.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely risky. It endangers you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers. Paying full attention to driving helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: It begins to rain while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Drive faster than surrounding traffic.
Drive at the posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive closely behind the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed when heavy rain reduces visibility. Turn on your headlights so other drivers can see you. If the rain is so heavy you cannot see clearly, pull to the shoulder and stop until it improves.
